title: Percentage Distribution of various IPC crimes during 1995-1997
pdf_title: Percentage Distribution of various IPC crimes during 1995-1997
notes: 1.3.1 The total cognizable crimes in the country had been steadily increasing. It is however keeping pace with the increase in population, though at varying rates, over the past 50 years. As many as 64,11,259 cognizable crimes were reported in the country during 1997. The incidence of total cognizable crimes in 1997 increased by 28.3 per cent over 1987 with a compound growth rate of 2.4 per cent per annum.
1.3.2 Reporting of IPC crimes recorded a marginal increase of 0.6 per cent in 1997 as compared, to 1996. Correspondingly, reporting of SLL crimes recorded an increase of 2.3 per cent.

1.3.3 Of the 64,11,259 total (IPC+SLL) cognizable crimes registered in the country during the year 1997, 63,24,972 (98.7%) were reported in the States (25) and the remaining 86,287 constituting 1.3 per cent of the total were reported in the Union Territories (7).

1.4.1 Population is one of the factors influencing crime incidence. There is a positive correlation between the growth in incidence and the population of the country. The rate of crime defined as the 'incidence of crime per lakh (1,00,000) of population' is universally taken as a more realistic indicator as it balances the effect of growth in population. The rate of total cognizable crimes in the country during 1997 was 671.2, an increase of 5.0 per cent over 1987 with a compound growth rate of 0.4 per cent per annum.

1.4.2 The average crime rate for total crimes (IPC + SLL) in the States was 672.7 which is slightly higher than the All-India average of 671.2. The crime rate of total cognizable crimes declined by 0.7 per cent over the previous year(1996). The crime rate in respect of IPC crimes decreased by 1.9 per cent and SLL crime rate by 0.2 per cent in this year (1997).

1.5.1 17,19,820 IPC crimes were reported in the country during 1997, as against 17,09,576 during 1996 recording a marginal increase of 0.6 per cent in this year. The decadal variation showed 22.2 per cent increase over 1987 with a compound growth rate of 1.8 per cent per annum. The percentage increase of these crimes in 1997 over the quinquennial average (Q.A.) of 1992-96 was 2.9 per cent, compared to the 2.6 per cent increase in 1996 over the Q.A. of 1991-95, and 2.9 per cent during 1995, over the Q.A. of 1990-94. The share of IPC crimes to total cognizable crimes in percentage terms during 1997, however, declined to 26.8 from 27.2 in 1996.
